meta.title: Build calculator data
meta.units: SI throughout: metres, kilograms, kg/m^3. Girths in metres. 1 in = 0.0254 m, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg.

status_vocabulary.measured: Taken with a tape, scale or scanner in a study or survey, or a statistic (percentile, mean) of such measurements.
status_vocabulary.official: Printed by the publisher or a licensed book (comics), or an official results record (sport).
status_vocabulary.reported: Stated by a magazine, fan site, the athlete, or a secondary source; not independently measured.
status_vocabulary.derived: Calculated by us or the researchers from other numbers (includes girths filled from a template, and picture-derived girths).
status_vocabulary.estimate: A modelled or assumed value with a stated range.
status_vocabulary.unknown: No source. Show "unknown"; do not invent.
status_vocabulary.disputed: Facts only (kept from the research): sources disagree. Builds never use it as a status; they set disputed: true and give a range.

build.name: display name
build.height_m / weight_kg: {value, status, source_keys, basis, range, disputed, value_basis?, other?}. range is [lo, hi] when sources disagree or a value is uncertain; value is the reference value used for calculation. other lists dated or alternative values.
build.girths: object with the seven sites chest, waist, arm_flexed, forearm, thigh, calf, neck. Each is a girth entry or {value_m: null, status: "unknown"}.
build.extra_girths: optional girths that do not match a site definition (e.g. arm_relaxed)
build.template: null if all seven girths are recorded, else {build_id, method, reason, pi_build_kg_m3, pi_template_kg_m3, outside_template_range}. Fill each missing girth from the template build; if the template also lacks it, use the template's own template. Label filled girths derived.
build.girth_basis_weight_kg: optional: weight to use for template scaling when part of the weight adds no girth (Wolverine's adamantium)
build.editions: optional (comics): each published height/weight pair; height and weight ranges must not be combined across editions
build.variants: optional (comics): other forms with their own height and weight (human alter egos etc.)
build.derived: BMI and W/H^3 from the reference values

girth_entry.value_m: reference value in metres (null if unknown)
girth_entry.value_basis: why value_m was chosen when disputed

template_methods.geometric: G = G_template x sqrt((W/H) / (W_template/H_template)): fixed shape (chest follows this in ANSUR II, exponent 1.02)
template_methods.isometric: G = G_template x (H / H_template): pure size scaling, same shape and same density
template_methods.ansur_predictor: G_cm = A x W_kg^p x H_m^q from ansur2_girth_predictor_male / _female: average soldier shape for that height and weight

values.orig: Allowable observer error (mm): chest 14, waist 12, biceps 6, forearm 5, thigh 6, calf 4, neck 6; weight 0.3 kg

ansur2_measurement_definitions.notes: Measurer's Handbook sec. 6.4: CHEST = horizontal at chest point anterior (fullest part of chest/bust), at the maximum point of QUIET respiration (not a puffed/expanded chest). WAIST (OMPHALION) = horizontal at the centre of the navel, abdomen not tensed; ANSUR II did NOT measure natural-waist (narrowest) circumference (TR-15/007 App. F lists natural-indentation waist only for ANSUR 1988), so omphalion waist runs larger than a 'natural waist' tape number. BICEPS FLEXED = right upper arm horizontal forward, elbow ~90 deg, fist clenched toward head, 'maximum effort in making a muscle', tape at highest point of flexed biceps, perpendicular to arm. FOREARM FLEXED = at the elbow crease, upper arm horizontal, elbow 90 deg, fist tightly clenched. THIGH = at the gluteal furrow (top of thigh), perpendicular to the thigh's long axis, thigh relaxed. LOWER THIGH = at suprapatella (just above knee). CALF = three readings in the region of maximum girth; the highest is kept (TR-15/007). NECK = at the infrathyroid landmark, the lowest point of the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple), perpendicular to the neck axis; NECK BASE is a separate, larger measure. Allowable observer error from Table G-1 (pp.224-227); these are allowable thresholds, not measured error. TR-15/007 reports measured inter-observer error separately (for example about 5.9 mm for waist).

TR-15/007 also reports the measured inter-observer error (for example about 5.9 mm for waist).

ansur2_girth_scaling_male.notes: Geometric expectation: if body SHAPE is fixed (isometric scaling, or widening at fixed height), every girth is proportional to sqrt(W/H), i.e. exponent b=1. Two fits per girth. (1) Proportional through the origin, G = k*X with X = sqrt(W[kg]/H[m]). k is a per-girth shape constant, and the per-subject percentiles of G/X show how much shape varies. R2 is measured against the mean of G and is negative for girths that barely track mass (wrist: -0.22 M, -0.17 F). (2) Free power law ln G = ln a + b ln X (OLS). Results: chest tracks the geometric law almost exactly (b about 1.02-1.04). Waist grows much faster than geometric (b about 1.4): in this population extra mass goes to the abdomen. Upper thigh and biceps grow a bit faster (b about 1.09-1.24). Lower thigh is about geometric (0.91 M, 1.02 F). Forearm, calf and neck grow slower (b about 0.62-0.85). These exponents describe how soldiers differ in size. ANSUR II has no body-composition data. By Forbes's relation (Hall 2007, Br J Nutr 97:1059, PMC2376748), at typical fat masses roughly 60-70% of between-person weight difference is fat (estimate, derived from data on women). They do NOT describe how a body changes when it adds muscle: a bodybuilder adds girth to arms, chest and thighs, not to the waist, so use them with care outside the sample. Also fitted: ln G = c + p ln W + q ln H (see ansur2_girth_predictor_male). All per-girth values are saved in fits.json.

rex_ollie_picture_girths.notes: Girth = Ramanujan ellipse perimeter of the measured frontal width w and depth k x w, at the picture's scale 0.0038582 m/px. k is the depth ratio the reconciled volume model used at that site: chest 1.05 (range 0.90-1.25), waist 0.80 (0.70-0.90), legs 1.0 (0.85-1.10), Rex upper arm 0.90, Ollie upper arm 0.95, forearm 0.85, Rex neck 1.05 (head-neck k), Ollie neck 1.0. Arm k ranges 0.80-1.00 (Rex) and 0.85-1.05 (Ollie), forearm 0.75-0.95 and neck +/-0.10 are assumptions made for this page. Ranges combine the width range with the k range. Method check on ANSUR II medians: from chest breadth 0.289 m at k 1.05 this construction gives 0.931 m vs a measured chest of 1.056 m (12% short); from waist breadth 0.325 m at k 0.80 it gives 0.922 vs 0.937 m (2% short).

build_templates_rule.label: How missing girths are filled (template choice)

methods.geometric: G = G_template x sqrt((W/H) / (W_template/H_template)): fixed shape (chest follows this in ANSUR II, exponent 1.02)
methods.isometric: G = G_template x (H / H_template): pure size scaling, same shape and same density
methods.ansur_predictor: G_cm = A x W_kg^p x H_m^q from ansur2_girth_predictor_male / _female: average soldier shape for that height and weight

values.rule: Same sex. Pick the shape class from the source (muscular hero or bodybuilder; heavy, thick-waisted; everyday). Within the class, pick the build with recorded girths whose W/H^3 is closest (log distance). Muscular class: Reeves, Mr America mean, de Moraes, Arnold, Oliva, Heath, Yates, Cutler, Coleman. Heavy class: ANSUR II largest-arm man. Female: ANSUR II women only (no female athlete girths exist in these data).

build_templates_rule.notes: Rule used by this page. Girths filled this way are derived. Builds with BMI above 43.45 (the highest BMI of any person with measured girths here, an ANSUR II man) are flagged as beyond human girth data. So are heights more than 10% outside the ANSUR II stature range (below 1.28 m or above 2.19 m), because the scaling law is checked only for height changes of about 10%.
